identity: Native baseline: IWIBench 0.2.6 at ff1bbcc78f6090e17bf4d50afeb7dc51437b3b53 pins Verifiers revision 5dad16d40e2d025672fdb7aa75b6540c0053e4e0. The run requires the null harness. Its taskset only accepts the development split and defaults to the 1B target, so explicitly select the pinned 4B revision and construct a separate training/outer-test schedule in the extension. TRL exposes a second, experimental HarborSpec and HarborEnv path. Pin its library version and source before deploying. [S1–S4]
information_and_action_parity: For evaluation, use the same typed service for an API-backed or open updater. For RL, have the open updater under training generate each turn and save sampled tokens and log-probabilities. TRL masks environment tokens and discovers tools from typed public methods on the HarborEnv subclass; expose only the intended tools. Installed, autonomous agents are opaque to this training loop. Give each sampled candidate equal accessible public examples, allowed operands, parameter scope, and limits. [S3]
observation_provenance: The existing setup passes objective, practice, manifest, relevant token IDs and limits into the prompt. The finalized trace logs session, patch, counters, tool names, revisions, error status, duration and aggregate metrics. Proposed extension: capture full schema-versioned actions, result digests, base revision, dictionary hash and probe IDs in the privileged trace store. The trace is audit evidence, not a future target input. [S1]
diagnostic_effect: Diagnostic logits, activations and public probe summaries can appear as tool observations. Mask returned tool texts in the updater's loss. For causal attribution, compare diagnostics with permuted evidence under equivalent compute and preserve the original verifier reward. A future reward-shaping study would be a separate objective. [S3]
edit_and_replay: IWIBench finalization invokes the worker's submit endpoint, collects the patch metadata and counters, and obtains a scalar from the grading endpoint with a finite [0,1] check. Proposed trainable rollout: branch each candidate from an identical starting checkpoint; freeze, hash and replay its numeric patch in a clean scoring process. Verify a scripted edit gives identical patch digest and raw target/control counts in the native, Harbor and trainer-driven paths before trusting downstream scores. [S1, S3, S4]
patch_quality: Keep the native reward and raw counts in the evaluation path. TRL HarborEnv selects named reward from the verifier's mapping, or its first value or zero if absent. Emit an explicit primary reward and surface missing or nonfinite results as infrastructure failures; retain detailed target, nearby, general and override counts separately. Keep gradient updates on the updater for outer RL and preserve clean target scoring. [S1, S3, S4]
updater_cost: Log policy input, cached input if known, output including reasoning when exposed, cost by provider, trainable token count, critic/reward overhead if used, trajectory wall time and sampled groups. The training token mask does not remove tool text from forward-pass context costs. Record failure/no-op trajectories and the fraction of zero-variance reward groups separately.
target_cost: Proposed instrumentation: one target session per rollout with a frozen common base and isolated patch, on a shared but serialized worker or separate workers with explicit scheduling. Charge all public probes, comparative branches, clean grading and idle allocation; count GPU-hours for updater generation/training independently from target execution. A fresh TRL environment per rollout does not itself establish isolation at a shared external target service. [S1, S3, S4]
uncertainty: [uncertain] Full RL compatibility with the exact pinned Verifiers/prime-rl versions and true separate-verifier behavior in TRL remain unverified end-to-end for this harness. The inspected TRL implementation constructs its verifier against self._env, routed through a factory; do not infer clean target replay from that call or public documentation alone. Test the installed stack with a known patch, a no-op and a failed patch. Published task results are benchmarks of editors, not results for a trained updater in this project. [S1, S3, S4, S5]
portability_and_terms: Prime-RL documents native integration with Verifiers environments. IWIBench's project metadata pins a specific Verifiers commit; avoid mixing v0/v1 APIs. TRL's Harbor integration is experimental and requires a reachable sandbox backend. Its published _env.py source has an Apache-2.0 header; prime-rl lists Apache-2.0; review exact component licenses before distribution. [S2–S5]
sequential_transfer: Proposed future sequence: one rollout owns a private target branch, carries only committed numeric updates across jobs, resets target chat and tools each job, and measures current and earlier skills. Outer policy training can use labeled development feedback after each rollout. Final evaluation needs independent streams that never influence policy optimization, checkpoint choice or candidate selection.
